title: Implicit leadership theories (leader prototype ratings)
instructions: Rate how characteristic each of the following is of a leader in general. Answer about leaders as a category — not about any specific person in this meeting.
anchors: not at all characteristic of a leader
citation: Offermann, L. R., & Coats, M. R. (2018). Implicit theories of leadership: Stability and change over two decades. The Leadership Quarterly, 29(4), 513-522. Items and factor assignments transcribed from Figure 2 (p.518), which prints all 46 items with their highest factor loadings. Femininity (female, feminine) and ethics (fair, honest, ethical) added as Sheng, Andrews & van Vugt (2026) did, per their footnote 13, giving the 51 items their Appendix (p.801) records for Study 5.
note: The instrument Sheng et al. actually administered, replacing the 1994 reconstruction kept at leader_ideal_1994.json. Three assignments differ from the 1994 version in ways that matter here: 'bold' is in CHARISMA, not strength (the 2018 discussion, p.520: 'the trait bold moved from the Strength factor from 1994 to the Charismatic factor'); STRENGTH is six command-and-assertion items rather than {strong, bold}; and 'attractive' sits in MASCULINITY while WELL-GROOMED keeps only well-groomed and well-dressed. predicts is unchanged in substance -- it is still Table 13's significant increments -- but now names the 2018 dimensions, so status reaches well_groomed rather than the 1994 'attractiveness', and vision reaches creativity, a dimension the reconstruction did not have.
